title: Rav Avira (II)
author: Aharon Hyman

paragraphs: He was a student of Rava and a colleague of Ravina. In Chullin 55a he spoke in the name of Rava, and in Bava Batra 131a he disagrees with Ravina in the name of Rava. In Pesachim 73a, "Ravina objected to it — Rav Avira said," etc. And in Ketubot 103a, he said to Ravina, "Is it comparable?"
As for what we find in Menachot 43a, "Rav Adda before Rava in the name of Rav Avira," one should read "Rav Avya," who was older than Rava (Dikdukei Soferim).
And we find Rav Acha son of Rav Avira in the time of Rav Ashi, as in Berakhot 44a.[^1][^2]

notes.text: Avira/Avya is Hyman’s proposed correction. The claim that the latter was older than Rava is not converted into a canonical identity merger.

Hyman proposes Avya for Avira in the Menachot passage, citing דק״ס, read here as Dikdukei Soferim. The reported age comparison belongs to that proposal. The final Berakhot locator has a double period, מד.., rendered as 44a.
